## Writes the prototype's placeholder sprites as PNGs. Every pixel comes from this code:
## flat cartoon colours plus a dark outline, no generated or downloaded art.
##   godot --headless --path godot --script res://tools/make_sprites.gd

const OUTLINE := Color("2b2b2b")
const OUT_DIR := "res://assets/sprites/"

# Named colours, so later work (shader predictions) can refer to exact source values.
const STRAW := Color("e9c46a")
const BURLAP := Color("d9b98a")
const POLE := Color("8b5a2b")
const HAT := Color("7a4e2d")
const PATCH := Color("b5651d")
const HOOD := Color("3a7d44")
const SKIN := Color("f1c27d")
const BOW := Color("6b3e1f")
const LEATHER := Color("5a3a22")
const CHEST := Color("9c6b3c")
const LID := Color("7a4e2d")
const GOLD := Color("e2b33c")
const WHITE := Color("f7f3e8")
const FLAME := Color("ff7a1a")
const STEEL := Color("9aa3ab")
const FLETCH := Color("c0392b")


func _init() -> void:
	DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(OUT_DIR))
	_save(_scarecrow(), "scarecrow.png")
	_save(_archer(), "archer.png")
	_save(_arrow(), "arrow.png")
	_save(_mimi(), "mimi.png")
	quit(0)


func _save(img: Image, file: String) -> void:
	var err := img.save_png(OUT_DIR + file)
	print("%s %s %dx%d" % ["wrote" if err == OK else "FAILED", file, img.get_width(), img.get_height()])


func _scarecrow() -> Image:
	var img := _blank(56, 72)
	_rect(img, 26, 30, 4, 40, POLE)            # pole
	_rect(img, 4, 30, 48, 4, POLE)             # cross-stick arms
	_rect(img, 2, 28, 5, 8, STRAW)             # straw tufts at the hands
	_rect(img, 49, 28, 5, 8, STRAW)
	_ellipse(img, 28, 46, 14, 16, STRAW)       # straw-stuffed body
	_rect(img, 31, 45, 6, 6, PATCH)            # sewn patch
	_ellipse(img, 28, 22, 11, 11, BURLAP)      # sack head
	_rect(img, 12, 12, 32, 4, HAT)             # hat brim
	_rect(img, 18, 2, 20, 11, HAT)             # hat crown
	_rect(img, 23, 20, 3, 3, OUTLINE)          # eyes
	_rect(img, 31, 20, 3, 3, OUTLINE)
	for x in range(23, 34, 2):                 # stitched mouth
		img.set_pixel(x, 27, OUTLINE)
	return _outlined(img)


func _archer() -> Image:
	# Seen from behind and below: the archer faces up the screen, toward the enemies.
	var img := _blank(44, 60)
	_rect(img, 14, 46, 6, 12, LEATHER)         # legs
	_rect(img, 24, 46, 6, 12, LEATHER)
	_ellipse(img, 22, 36, 12, 13, HOOD)        # cloak
	_rect(img, 10, 40, 24, 3, LEATHER)         # belt
	_ellipse(img, 22, 16, 10, 11, HOOD)        # hood
	_rect(img, 18, 24, 8, 4, SKIN)             # neck
	_rect(img, 33, 4, 3, 44, BOW)              # bow stave
	_rect(img, 36, 6, 1, 40, WHITE)            # bowstring
	return _outlined(img)


func _arrow() -> Image:
	var img := _blank(10, 30)
	_rect(img, 4, 6, 2, 20, POLE)              # shaft
	_rect(img, 3, 2, 4, 5, STEEL)              # head
	_rect(img, 4, 0, 2, 3, FLAME)              # fire tip
	_rect(img, 2, 24, 2, 5, FLETCH)            # fletching
	_rect(img, 6, 24, 2, 5, FLETCH)
	return _outlined(img)


func _mimi() -> Image:
	var img := _blank(76, 60)
	_rect(img, 6, 26, 64, 30, CHEST)           # chest body
	_rect(img, 6, 6, 64, 14, LID)              # lid, raised a little: Mimi is peeking
	_rect(img, 6, 20, 64, 6, OUTLINE)          # dark mouth gap
	for x in range(10, 68, 8):                 # teeth
		_rect(img, x, 20, 4, 3, WHITE)
	_ellipse(img, 26, 13, 5, 5, WHITE)         # eyes on the lid
	_ellipse(img, 50, 13, 5, 5, WHITE)
	_rect(img, 25, 13, 3, 3, OUTLINE)
	_rect(img, 49, 13, 3, 3, OUTLINE)
	_rect(img, 14, 26, 5, 30, GOLD)            # gold bands
	_rect(img, 57, 26, 5, 30, GOLD)
	_rect(img, 33, 30, 10, 10, GOLD)           # lock
	_rect(img, 37, 33, 2, 4, OUTLINE)
	return _outlined(img)


func _blank(w: int, h: int) -> Image:
	var img := Image.create(w, h, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
	img.fill(Color(0, 0, 0, 0))
	return img


func _rect(img: Image, x: int, y: int, w: int, h: int, c: Color) -> void:
	img.fill_rect(Rect2i(x, y, w, h), c)


func _ellipse(img: Image, cx: int, cy: int, rx: int, ry: int, c: Color) -> void:
	for y in range(cy - ry, cy + ry + 1):
		for x in range(cx - rx, cx + rx + 1):
			var dx := float(x - cx) / rx
			var dy := float(y - cy) / ry
			if dx * dx + dy * dy <= 1.0 and x >= 0 and y >= 0 and x < img.get_width() and y < img.get_height():
				img.set_pixel(x, y, c)


## Adds a 1-pixel dark outline around every opaque pixel (4-neighbour), in place.
func _outlined(img: Image) -> Image:
	var src := img.duplicate() as Image
	for y in img.get_height():
		for x in img.get_width():
			if src.get_pixel(x, y).a > 0.0:
				continue
			for d in [Vector2i(1, 0), Vector2i(-1, 0), Vector2i(0, 1), Vector2i(0, -1)]:
				var p: Vector2i = Vector2i(x, y) + d
				if p.x >= 0 and p.y >= 0 and p.x < img.get_width() and p.y < img.get_height() and src.get_pixelv(p).a > 0.0:
					img.set_pixel(x, y, OUTLINE)
					break
	return img

## Meadow, castle wall and gate, drawn in code (flat cartoon colours).

const MEADOW := Color("6da34d")
const TUFT := Color("5a8f3e")
const STONE := Color("8d8f94")
const MORTAR := Color("6f7176")
const WALKWAY := Color("a3a5aa")
const GATE := Color("3b2f2a")


func _draw() -> void:
	var w := Tuning.VIEW.x
	var top := Tuning.WALL_TOP
	draw_rect(Rect2(0, 0, w, Tuning.VIEW.y), MEADOW)
	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
	rng.seed = 7                                   # same tufts every run
	for i in 70:
		var p := Vector2(rng.randf_range(0, w), rng.randf_range(0, top - 40))
		draw_line(p, p + Vector2(-3, -7), TUFT, 2.0)
		draw_line(p, p + Vector2(3, -8), TUFT, 2.0)
	draw_rect(Rect2(0, top, w, Tuning.VIEW.y - top), STONE)
	draw_rect(Rect2(0, top - 4, w, 10), WALKWAY)
	for row in 4:                                  # brick courses
		var y := top + 6 + row * 28.0
		draw_line(Vector2(0, y), Vector2(w, y), MORTAR, 2.0)
		var offset := 0.0 if row % 2 == 0 else 32.0
		var x := offset
		while x < w:
			draw_line(Vector2(x, y), Vector2(x, y + 28), MORTAR, 2.0)
			x += 64.0
	draw_rect(Rect2(596, top + 34, 88, Tuning.VIEW.y - top - 34), GATE)
	draw_circle(Vector2(640, top + 34), 44, GATE)

func _arrow() -> Image:

func _mimi() -> Image:

	_rect(img, 6, 26, 64, 30, CHEST)           # chest body
	_rect(img, 6, 6, 64, 14, LID)              # lid, raised a little: Mimi is peeking

	for x in range(10, 68, 8):                 # teeth
		_rect(img, x, 20, 4, 3, WHITE)
	_ellipse(img, 26, 13, 5, 5, WHITE)         # eyes on the lid
	_ellipse(img, 50, 13, 5, 5, WHITE)
	_rect(img, 25, 13, 3, 3, OUTLINE)

	_rect(img, 57, 26, 5, 30, GOLD)
	_rect(img, 33, 30, 10, 10, GOLD)           # lock
	_rect(img, 37, 33, 2, 4, OUTLINE)

func _blank(w: int, h: int) -> Image:
	var img := Image.create(w, h, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
	img.fill(Color(0, 0, 0, 0))
	return img


func _rect(img: Image, x: int, y: int, w: int, h: int, c: Color) -> void:
	img.fill_rect(Rect2i(x, y, w, h), c)


func _ellipse(img: Image, cx: int, cy: int, rx: int, ry: int, c: Color) -> void:
	for y in range(cy - ry, cy + ry + 1):
		for x in range(cx - rx, cx + rx + 1):
			var dx := float(x - cx) / rx
			var dy := float(y - cy) / ry
			if dx * dx + dy * dy <= 1.0 and x >= 0 and y >= 0 and x < img.get_width() and y < img.get_height():
				img.set_pixel(x, y, c)


## Adds a 1-pixel dark outline around every opaque pixel (4-neighbour), in place.
func _outlined(img: Image) -> Image:
	var src := img.duplicate() as Image
	for y in img.get_height():
		for x in img.get_width():
			if src.get_pixel(x, y).a > 0.0:
				continue
			for d in [Vector2i(1, 0), Vector2i(-1, 0), Vector2i(0, 1), Vector2i(0, -1)]:
				var p: Vector2i = Vector2i(x, y) + d
				if p.x >= 0 and p.y >= 0 and p.x < img.get_width() and p.y < img.get_height() and src.get_pixelv(p).a > 0.0:
					img.set_pixel(x, y, OUTLINE)
					break
	return img

class_name Scarecrow
extends Node2D
## Straw Scarecrow: walks down to the wall and hits the gate. Straw burns.
## Owns the Burning state: burn_time_left > 0 means burning. Fire refreshes it to the full
## BURN_DURATION (a second hit does not stack damage). Timed in physics time, so it follows
## Engine.time_scale and stops while the tree is paused.

signal burning_started
signal burning_ended
signal died
signal attacking_gate(amount: float)

const BURN_END_EPSILON := 1e-9      # s; float residue below this counts as burnt out

var hp: float = Tuning.SCARECROW_HP
var burn_time_left: float = 0.0
var at_wall := false


func _ready() -> void:
	add_to_group("enemies")
	at_wall = position.y >= Tuning.SCARECROW_STOP_Y


func is_burning() -> bool:
	return burn_time_left > 0.0


func is_dead() -> bool:
	return hp <= 0.0


func hit(damage: float, element: StringName) -> void:
	if is_dead():
		return
	hp -= damage
	if element == &"fire":
		ignite()
	_check_death()


func ignite() -> void:
	var was_burning := is_burning()
	burn_time_left = Tuning.BURN_DURATION
	if not was_burning:
		burning_started.emit()


func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if is_dead() or is_queued_for_deletion():   # a reset in the same tick must not hit the gate
		return
	if is_burning():
		var burned := minf(delta, burn_time_left)
		hp -= Tuning.BURN_DPS * burned
		burn_time_left -= delta
		# Summing 240 deltas of 1/60 leaves ~1e-14 instead of 0, which used to add a 241st tick.
		if burn_time_left <= BURN_END_EPSILON:
			burn_time_left = 0.0
			burning_ended.emit()
		_check_death()
		if is_dead():
			return
	if at_wall:
		attacking_gate.emit(Tuning.SCARECROW_GATE_DPS * delta)
	else:
		position.y = minf(position.y + Tuning.SCARECROW_SPEED * delta, Tuning.SCARECROW_STOP_Y)
		at_wall = position.y >= Tuning.SCARECROW_STOP_Y


func _check_death() -> void:
	if is_dead():
		remove_from_group("enemies")
		died.emit()
		queue_free()

	root.add_child(game)

##   bash scripts/run-test.sh test_impact_burst_config.gd 60
## Prints one PASS/FAIL line per check and exits 1 on any failure. Headless: this proves the
## configuration, not the look (CLAUDE.md, headless facts).

const SCENE_PATH := "res://effects/impact_burst.tscn"
const EPS := 1e-4
const COLOR_EPS := 1e-3          # colours are stored as 32-bit floats

var passed := 0
var failed := 0


func _initialize() -> void:
	_run.call_deferred()


func _run() -> void:
	var packed := load(SCENE_PATH) as PackedScene
	_check("scene loads", packed != null, SCENE_PATH)
	if packed == null:
		_finish()
		return
	var burst := packed.instantiate()
	root.add_child(burst)
	await process_frame

func _check_emitter(node: Node, x: Dictionary) -> void:
	var n: String = x.name
	_check("%s exists as GPUParticles2D" % n, node is GPUParticles2D, "got %s" % (node.get_class() if node else "null"))
	if not node is GPUParticles2D:
		return
	var p := node as GPUParticles2D

	# Node: emission and simulation settings.
	_check("%s emitting = false" % n, p.emitting == false)
	_check("%s amount = %d" % [n, x.amount], p.amount == x.amount, str(p.amount))
	_check("%s one_shot = true" % n, p.one_shot == true)
	_eq("%s explosiveness" % n, p.explosiveness, 1.0)
	_eq("%s lifetime" % n, p.lifetime, x.lifetime)
	_eq("%s preprocess" % n, p.preprocess, 0.0)
	_check("%s local_coords = false" % n, p.local_coords == false)
	_check("%s visibility_rect = %s" % [n, x.vis], p.visibility_rect.is_equal_approx(x.vis), str(p.visibility_rect))
	_eq("%s amount_ratio (not used by A)" % n, p.amount_ratio, 1.0)

	# Draw: texture and blend mode.
	var tex := p.texture
	_check("%s texture = %s" % [n, x.texture], tex != null and tex.resource_path == x.texture,
			tex.resource_path if tex else "null")
	if tex:
		_check("%s texture size %s" % [n, x.tex_size], Vector2i(tex.get_size()) == x.tex_size, str(tex.get_size()))
	var cim := p.material as CanvasItemMaterial
	_check("%s material is CanvasItemMaterial" % n, cim != null, str(p.material))
	if cim:
		_check("%s blend_mode = %d" % [n, x.blend], cim.blend_mode == x.blend, str(cim.blend_mode))

	# Process: ParticleProcessMaterial.
	var m := p.process_material as ParticleProcessMaterial
	_check("%s process_material is ParticleProcessMaterial" % n, m != null, str(p.process_material))
	if m == null:
		return
	# Every property read below must be a stored property in 4.7.2, not an editor-only alias.
	for prop in ["particle_flag_disable_z", "emission_shape", "emission_sphere_radius", "direction", "spread",
			"gravity", "initial_velocity_min", "initial_velocity_max", "damping_min", "damping_max",
			"scale_min", "scale_max", "angle_min", "angle_max", "color_ramp", "scale_curve", "turbulence_enabled"]:
		_check("%s %s is a stored property" % [n, prop], _is_stored(m, prop))
	_check("%s particle_flag_disable_z = true" % n, m.particle_flag_disable_z == true)
	_check("%s emission_shape = SPHERE" % n, m.emission_shape == ParticleProcessMaterial.EMISSION_SHAPE_SPHERE,
			str(m.emission_shape))
	_eq("%s emission_sphere_radius" % n, m.emission_sphere_radius, x.radius)
	_check("%s direction = (0, -1, 0)" % n, m.direction.is_equal_approx(Vector3(0, -1, 0)), str(m.direction))
	_eq("%s spread" % n, m.spread, x.spread)
	_check("%s gravity = %s" % [n, x.gravity], m.gravity.is_equal_approx(x.gravity), str(m.gravity))
	_eq("%s initial_velocity_min" % n, m.initial_velocity_min, x.vel[0])
	_eq("%s initial_velocity_max" % n, m.initial_velocity_max, x.vel[1])
	_eq("%s damping_min" % n, m.damping_min, x.damping[0])
	_eq("%s damping_max" % n, m.damping_max, x.damping[1])
	_eq("%s scale_min" % n, m.scale_min, x.scale[0])
	_eq("%s scale_max" % n, m.scale_max, x.scale[1])
	_eq("%s angle_min" % n, m.angle_min, x.angle[0])
	_eq("%s angle_max" % n, m.angle_max, x.angle[1])
	_check("%s turbulence_enabled = false (not used by A)" % n, m.turbulence_enabled == false)

	# Colour ramp.
	var gt := m.color_ramp as GradientTexture1D
	_check("%s color_ramp is GradientTexture1D" % n, gt != null and gt.gradient != null, str(m.color_ramp))
	if gt and gt.gradient:
		var g := gt.gradient
		_check("%s color ramp has %d stops" % [n, x.ramp_offsets.size()],
				g.get_point_count() == x.ramp_offsets.size(), str(g.get_point_count()))
		for i in mini(g.get_point_count(), x.ramp_offsets.size()):
			_eq("%s ramp stop %d offset" % [n, i], g.get_offset(i), x.ramp_offsets[i])
			_check("%s ramp stop %d colour %s" % [n, i, x.ramp_colors[i]],
					_color_close(g.get_color(i), x.ramp_colors[i]), str(g.get_color(i)))

	# Scale curve.
	var ct := m.scale_curve as CurveTexture
	_check("%s scale_curve is CurveTexture" % n, ct != null and ct.curve != null, str(m.scale_curve))
	if ct and ct.curve:
		var c := ct.curve
		_eq("%s Curve.max_value" % n, c.max_value, x.curve_max)
		_check("%s scale curve has %d points" % [n, x.curve_points.size()],
				c.point_count == x.curve_points.size(), str(c.point_count))
		for i in mini(c.point_count, x.curve_points.size()):
			_check("%s scale curve point %d = %s" % [n, i, x.curve_points[i]],
					c.get_point_position(i).is_equal_approx(x.curve_points[i]), str(c.get_point_position(i)))


# --- helpers -----------------------------------------------------------------

func _check(name: String, ok: bool, detail: String = "") -> void:
	if ok:
		passed += 1
		print("PASS %s" % name)
	else:
		failed += 1
		print("FAIL %s  %s" % [name, detail])


func _eq(name: String, got: float, want: float) -> void:
	_check("%s = %s" % [name, want], absf(got - want) <= EPS, "got %s" % got)


func _color_close(a: Color, b: Color) -> bool:
	return absf(a.r - b.r) <= COLOR_EPS and absf(a.g - b.g) <= COLOR_EPS \
			and absf(a.b - b.b) <= COLOR_EPS and absf(a.a - b.a) <= COLOR_EPS


func _is_stored(obj: Object, prop: String) -> bool:
	for p in obj.get_property_list():
		if p.name == prop:
			return (p.usage & PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE) != 0
	return false

I built Effect A as a scene, added its configuration test and a preview scene. The configuration test passes 128/0 at 60. Nothing is wired into gameplay, no `.gdshader` file was touched, and nothing is committed.

## Files added
- **`godot/tools/make_particle_textures.gd`**: the brief says the particle textures come from committed code. This script writes `godot/effects/textures/soft_dot.png` (16×16, a white dot that fades at the edge) and `straw_chip.png` (4×12, a narrow white chip). The colour ramps tint them. I ran it and then ran `--import`. The smoke texture is for Effect B, so I didn't add it yet.
- **`godot/effects/impact_burst.tscn`**: a root `ImpactBurst` (Node2D) holding two GPUParticles2D emitters, `Flash` (A1) and `Straw` (A2). Every setting from §3 is in the scene file, with each emitter's ParticleProcessMaterial, Gradient/GradientTexture1D, Curve/CurveTexture and CanvasItemMaterial as sub-resources. There is no script.
- **`godot/tests/test_impact_burst_config.gd`**: loads the scene and reads every §3 value back from the loaded nodes and resources. It also checks that each material property it reads has `PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE`, so a Godot 3 name or an editor-only alias would fail. Extra checks: turbulence is off, `amount_ratio` is 1.0 (Effect A uses neither), straw outlives flash (Rule A5), and neither emitter is emitting one frame after loading.
- **`godot/previews/impact_burst_preview.tscn` + `.gd`**: the game's own background (`background.gd`) at 1:1 scale (the game has no Camera2D), a still scarecrow sprite at (640, 530), and an `Effects` node. It fires at frame 10, and again at frame 28 when `retrigger` is on (the default; pass `-- --no-retrigger` to turn it off). Each hit creates a new burst instance, which frees itself when its straw emitter finishes.

## Things I couldn't verify
- **Curve format:** I wanted a short Godot script to show how 4.7.2 saves a `Curve` with `max_value`, but running it was denied. So I wrote `max_value = 1.5` before `_data` by hand.
